stances.claim: The concurring opinions of Perlas-Bernabe and Jardeleza represent the most jurisprudentially significant contributions: their sui generis standard (placing the burden of proof on the government, not petitioners) and the 'reasonableness' test (not probable cause) will be pivotal when future ML declarations or extensions are challenged.
stances.rhetorical_move: prospective-relevance argument: flagging minority doctrinal positions as future governing standards

stances.claim: Sereno's and Carpio's opinions are mischaracterized as 'Dissenting' when they actually concurred on the factual basis of P216 but dissented only on territorial coverage — they should properly be titled 'Concurring and Dissenting,' and their mislabeling causes valuable legal gems in those opinions to be overlooked.
stances.rhetorical_move: taxonomic-correction argument: proper opinion classification as a precondition for doctrinal uptake

stances.claim: Leonen's 92-page dissent — arguing that the Court cannot grant undefined ML powers over all of Mindanao and that ML as proclaimed is vague and thus unconstitutional — is the only true dissent and deserves to be 'read and reread,' because its 'peregrinations may be lonely now but could be cheerful at another time.'
stances.rhetorical_move: minority-vindication prophecy: the lonely dissent as a seed for future jurisprudential reversal
stances.confidence: asserted with temporal hedge ('at another time')

notable_anecdotes: CJ Panganiban's opening framing of the 14 opinions as 'indigestible legal gobbledygook for lay people' but a 'veritable legal feast for law scholars' — a rare self-aware acknowledgment that the column is deliberately written for legal specialists, not the lay audience he usually targets.

The taxonomic correction of Sereno's and Carpio's opinions: both labeled 'Dissenting' in the official reports but actually 'Concurring and Dissenting' in substance — CJ notes this not as pedantry but because the mislabeling buries their 'legal gems' (Sereno's comprehensive arrest/seizure rights dissertation, Carpio's four ML consequences) which the majority could and should have adopted.

The elegant prophecy for Leonen's lone 92-page dissent: 'His peregrinations may be lonely now, but they could be cheerful at another time' — a classic CJ Panganiban rhetorical move of validating the dissenter's intellectual courage while suggesting that jurisprudential history may yet vindicate him.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens by acknowledging that the 14 separate opinions in Lagman vs Medialdea (July 4, 2017) constitute 'indigestible legal gobbledygook for lay people' but a 'veritable legal feast for law scholars,' and proceeds to curate the most jurisprudentially significant contributions. He highlights the concurrences of Perlas-Bernabe and Jardeleza, which argued that ML review is sui generis: the government, not the petitioners, bears the burden of proving the sufficiency of facts because only the government has access to classified information, and the applicable standard is 'reasonableness' rather than the ponencia's 'probable cause' -- with all four ordinary judicial review thresholds (substantial evidence, preponderance, proof beyond reasonable doubt, grave abuse of discretion) to be discarded. He then makes a taxonomic correction: Sereno's and Carpio's opinions -- which concurred on P216's factual basis but dissented only on territorial coverage (Lanao/Maguindanao/Sulu for Sereno with Caguioa; Marawi-only for Carpio) -- are mislabeled as 'Dissenting' and should be 'Concurring and Dissenting,' since their mislabeling buries valuable 'legal gems': Sereno's comprehensive dissertation on arrest/seizure procedures and rights of the accused, and Carpio's four-consequence taxonomy of ML. Finally, he identifies Leonen's 92-page opus as the only true dissent, recommending it be 'read and reread' for its holding that the Court cannot grant the President undefined ML powers over all of Mindanao and its application of the 'void for vagueness' and 'void for overbreadth' doctrines -- predicting with characteristic elegance that Leonen's 'peregrinations may be lonely now, but they could be cheerful at another time.'
